description: ICON is a passionate and ambitious team participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge in Cairo. We believe in innovation, teamwork, and turning real-world challenges into creative solutions using technology and science. Our interests include AI, software development, hardware, data analysis, and space exploration. We welcome motivated and creative members who want to learn, collaborate, and build something impactful together.
summary:
TerraAnalog is a web app by Team ICON for NASA Space Apps Cairo 2026. It finds places on Earth whose terrain matches sites on Mars and the Moon, so rovers can be tested on Earth before going to space.
Enter any coordinates or upload a .hgt elevation file, and the app shows synchronized Earth, Mars, and Moon maps, a 3D terrain model, ranked analog matches, and gravity-aware rover stability results.
It uses Copernicus elevation data for Earth and NASA MOLA/LOLA-calibrated catalogs for Mars and the Moon. It is bilingual (Arabic/English), tested, and certified ready to deploy.

TerraAnalog: Project Details

Basic Information

  • Project name: TerraAnalog (v5.2)
  • Tagline: Planetary Terrain Intelligence & Analog Site Finder
  • Team: ICON (Ahmed Elsayed Ezzat, Areej Bahaa Eldin Elsayed, Youssef Mohamed Rabie, Hams Haitham Mohamed, Waad Hefny Abdelhafez, Mohamed Ahmed)
  • Event: NASA Space Apps Cairo 2026
  • Challenge: Identify Earth Locations that Analog the Permanent Moon Base Locations and Mars
  • Live app: https://areejbahaa33-code.github.io/TerraAnalog/

Problem Statement

Testing rovers and hardware for Mars and the Moon requires Earth sites with similar terrain. Today this is costly (remote field trials), slow (manual literature searches), and not gravity-aware (Mars gravity is 3.72 m/s² and Moon gravity is 1.62 m/s², which change rover behavior). No fast, open tool matches Earth sites to lunar and Martian terrain.

Solution

TerraAnalog compares the terrain of any Earth location with Mars and Moon reference catalogs and returns ranked analog matches in real time. It works in both directions: from an Earth site to Mars/Moon analogs, and from a Mars/Moon target (for example Jezero crater) back to the best Earth analogs.

Main Features

  1. Synchronized mapping: Three Leaflet maps (Earth, Mars, Moon) move in lockstep. Analyzing an Earth site makes the Mars and Moon maps fly to its closest analogs.
  2. 3D terrain mesh: A Three.js viewer shows the elevation model with rotation, wireframe, and auto-spin, alongside slope, roughness, and relief metrics.
  3. Analog cards and radar chart: Each match shows its similarity score, and clicking a card retargets the maps and metrics.
  4. Reverse targeting: Choose a Mars or Moon site and find the best Earth twins.
  5. Rover stability physics: Enter rover mass and center of gravity to see rollover safety margins under each planet’s gravity.
  6. Hardware readiness matrix and delta table: Compare slope, roughness, relief, gravity, maximum and minimum temperature, pressure, and radiation between environments.
  7. Local DEM upload: Users can upload their own .hgt elevation tile.
  8. Exports: CSV, JSON, and a printable Dossier.
  9. Voice briefing: A guided spoken tour of the page.
  10. Bilingual interface: Arabic and English with live RTL/LTR layout switching and 76 matched translation keys.

How the Analysis Works

  1. The user enters coordinates (the default is the Afar region, Ethiopia, at 13.5, 40.6) or uploads a .hgt file.
  2. The app samples an 8x8 elevation grid at about 275 m spacing (a ~2 km window) from Copernicus DEM GLO-90 via Open-Meteo.
  3. It computes slope, roughness, and relief.
  4. These values are compared with Mars and Moon reference catalogs built from 463 m cells, calibrated to NASA MOLA (Mars, native 463.09 m) and LRO LOLA (Moon, native 118.45 m resampled).
  5. The app returns ranked analogs with similarity percentages. Example from the demo: coordinates (42.35°, 64.45°) matched Mars #1 Elysium Planitia at 97.6% and Moon #1 Mare Tranquillitatis at 97.3%.

Technical Architecture

  • Front end: index.html (interface), style.css (dark glassmorphic styling), app.js (map sync, 3D renderer, voice tour, CSV export), i18n.js (separate English and Arabic dictionaries).
  • Engine: terra_engine_logic_only.js (logic, ~14 KB) and planetary_db.json (database, 283 KB) are merged by build_engine.py into terra_engine.js, which is never edited by hand.
  • Utilities: read_hgt_dem.py converts binary SRTM tiles to CSV/JSON; validate_data.py checks the data.
  • Reference data: all_cells_463m.csv, top_mars.csv/geojson, top_moon.csv/geojson, ref_sources.csv.
  • Docs: README.md, DATA_INDEX.md, SYNC_REPORT.md.
  • Libraries: Leaflet (maps) and Three.js (3D).

Testing and Audit

The v5.2 certification audit (November 14, 2026) returned “CERTIFIED TO DEPLOY: GO” with no regressions:

  • Engine rebuild is byte-identical to the shipped file.
  • 72 automated tests pass, 0 fail.
  • Data validation: 0 errors, 1 intentional warning.
  • No duplicate IDs, all inline handlers defined, identical English and Arabic key sets.
  • No overlap between map controls and overlays in RTL or LTR.

Scores: code quality 9.5, performance and robustness 9.5, UI/UX and bilingual support 9.0, science and data integrity 9.5, documentation 9.0. Overall: 9.3/10. The audit was static; one visual check in a browser is recommended before the demo.
